lots.title: (1) Johnnie Walker Red Label Blended Scotch Whisky, Scotland, 375ml, 42.3% ABV (Bottled in NZ) (TOL)
lots.what_it_really_is: Old New Zealand-bottled Johnnie Walker Red Label 'Old Scotch Whisky' in a 375ml flask, 74 proof, bottled by The Distillers Co. (N.Z.) Ltd., Auckland, with metal screw cap and Highest Awards strip label. Proof marking alongside a metric 375ml contents suggests roughly the 1970s, but that dating is my inference from the label, not printed on it.
lots.what_the_title_misses: The title is accurate (74 proof = 42.3% ABV; 'Bottled in NZ' is stated) but gives no era and does not name the DCL (NZ) Auckland bottler or the flask format. The value effect is uncertain: no sale of this bottling was found.
lots.photo_evidence: Read myself from 382910_1 and _2 with enlarged crops. Front label: '74 PROOF', 'PRODUCE OF SCOTLAND', 'CONTENTS 375 ml', 'Johnnie Walker Red Label Old Scotch Whisky', 'JOHN WALKER & SONS LTD., KILMARNOCK, SCOTLAND', 'BOTTLED IN NEW ZEALAND THE DISTILLERS CO. (N.Z.) LTD., AUCKLAND'. Lower strip: 'HIGHEST AWARDS', 'SYDNEY 1880 MELBOURNE 1881 PARIS 1885 ADELAIDE 1887 DUNEDIN 1890 KIMBERLEY 1892' (the Brisbane entry and right end are scraped away), 'GUARANTEED SAME QUALITY THROUGHOUT THE WORLD', striding man, 'John Walker & Sons Limited'. Neck label: royal arms, legible bottom line 'JOHN WALKER AND SONS LTD.', side text partly legible ('Scotch Whisky Distillers'), the appointment wording too worn to read reliably. Cap: red top, gold sleeve with 'John Walker' script and 'PAT. No' (digits unreadable); 382910_3 shows a grey scuff or patch on the sleeve. Fill (382910_3): liquid at base of neck, a good fill for age. The scan's 'no barcode seen' is right for the visible faces only; no back view was supplied. Front label has gold-foil wear and staining.
lots.condition: Fill at base of neck. Labels worn and tarnished, scraped patch on right of awards strip, scuffed cap sleeve. Back of bottle not photographed.
lots.guide_summary: No SOLD, UNSOLD or ASKING evidence for this bottling (NZ-bottled 375ml flask) survives. Every comp offered was a different bottling, most 4 to 10 years old.
lots.working: No same-bottling SOLD entry in the last 24 months, so keep and flip are both 0. Any bid is unsupported by evidence; ordinary old Red Label in other formats has sold from about GBP 15 to GBP 55 hammer, but that is a different bottling and is shown only as background, not as a value. Shipping to Australia adds freight, duty and GST.
lots.confidence_reason: Label read clearly, but there is no matching SOLD entry at all.
lots.dropped_entries: All eight comps dropped as not the same bottling (I opened every page on 2026-10-13 and confirmed the figures): Whisky.Auction 136783 GBP 55 (1L Fenton Hill duty free 43.4%, 2022-08-02); Whisky.Auction 98624 GBP 330 (1930s 75cl, 2021-01-19); SWA 064-3382 GBP 210 (1930s, no stated size, 2016-08-07); SWA 073-4291 GBP 20 (modern 19cl 43%, 2017-05-07; the draft gave the lot number as 150064, which is the URL id); SWA 079-2157 GBP 15 (70cl 40%, 2017-11-05; draft lot number 178004 was the URL id); SWA 080-5174 GBP 260 (1.75L with handle, 2017-12-03); Mizunara HKD 1,390 ASKING (Japan-market 760ml 43%); Reserved Treasures Club EUR 250 ASKING (1960s 70cl). On Whisky.Auction the 'Reserve Not met' wording the draft flagged is a hidden template badge on every lot page, not a result status, so it was not the reason to drop.
lots.question_for_webbs: Please explain the (TOL) code and send photos of the back of the bottle (any back label, importer or excise stamp), the cap seal from above to show it is unbroken, and a backlit fill shot. Is anything printed on the base giving a bottling year?

lots.title: (1) Johnnie Walker Blue Label 'Legendary Eight' 200th Anniversary Special Blended Scotch Whisky, Scotland, 43.8% ABV, 1000ml (GB)
lots.what_it_really_is: Johnnie Walker Blue Label Legendary Eight, 200th Anniversary Exclusive Blend (2020 release), 1L, 43.8%, with marbled blue presentation box. Matches the title.
lots.what_the_title_misses: Only the eight component distilleries on the box side (Oban, Lagavulin, Teaninich, Brora, Cambus, Port Dundas, Carsebridge, Blair Athol) and the 'ghost distilleries' back text. That is the defining, widely known feature of this release and is implied by the name, so it is not hidden value.
lots.photo_evidence: Read myself. Front label: 'BLUE LABEL Legendary Eight', '200TH ANNIVERSARY EXCLUSIVE BLEND', '1L' at lower left and '43.8%' at lower right, 'BOTTLE NO' with a number that is not reliably readable (enhanced crop suggests a two-letter prefix and five digits, possibly 'GX00?07'; I will not report it as read, and the earlier drafts' 'EX or EU' guess is not supported). Box front: 'ESTD 1820', 'A rare jewel crafted from only eight legendary distilleries, all at least 200 years old'; box spine lists the eight distilleries. Back: ghost distilleries text, stopper medallion with tassel. Shoulder: royal warrant 'By appointment to Her Majesty the Queen'. KEY FINDING: the three photos for lot 1333 (383660) and lot 1332 (383661) are byte-identical files (same MD5), so Webb's has used one set of photos for both lots. At most one of the two lots is the bottle pictured; the photos do not evidence the specific bottle, bottle number, box condition or fill of the other. Fill cannot be seen through the dark glass in any photo, so the scan's 'fill in neck' claim for 1332 is not supported.
lots.condition: Box and bottle look clean in the shared photos. Fill not visible. Condition of the actual bottle in this lot not verified because the photos are shared with the other lot.

lots.guide_summary: Same edition 70cl SOLD in last 24 months: GBP 210 (SWA, Sep 2026) and GBP 230 (Whisky.Auction, Jan 2025) hammer, NZD 571 to 625 in price-realised terms. Older 2024 results GBP 180. No 1L result anywhere. Launch retail USD 350; Australian retail AUD 499 (750ml, sold out).
lots.working: Comps are the same edition but 70cl, not 1L; no 1L SOLD exists. I use the 70cl prices unscaled (a 1L should not realise less, but no volume uplift is assumed). Keep: lowest in-window SOLD = GBP 210 hammer + 15% commission = GBP 241.50 x 2.3637 = NZD 570.83 (premium included, VAT excluded); 570.83 / 1.22425 = 466.27, rounded down to NZD 465 hammer (NZD 569 all-in at Webb's). Flip: likely resale = midpoint of the two in-window price-realised figures (GBP 241.50 and 264.50) = GBP 253 = NZD 598.02; less 15% = 508.32; / 2.4485 = 207.60, rounded down to NZD 205. Shipping from NZ to Australia adds freight, Australian excise duty and GST, not included.
lots.confidence_reason: Label text read and two in-window SOLD pages opened, but they are 70cl not 1L, and the photos are shared with another lot so this specific bottle is not evidenced. Not High.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped: Whisky.Auction 160032 (standard Blue Label 100cl, not Legendary Eight) and 187004 (standard Blue Label 175cl): different bottlings. Whisky Hammer 175228: page returns 403 to me too, a GBP 180 bid in a snippet is not a confirmed result. Wine-Searcher 6 x 1L USD 699.99: snippet only, not opened, listing incoherent. whiskyforeveryone launch GBP 275: page 403, snippet only. No UNSOLD evidence found (the earlier placeholder 'UNSOLD none found' row is not evidence and is removed). Extra search for any 1L or 100cl Legendary Eight result on 2026-10-13 found none.

Confirm it is the 1L pack and whether any customs or strip stamp is present.
